situation: A friend asks to borrow 20,000 rupees, and you do not want to lend it.
say: Yaar, actually, I'm a bit tight this month, maybe later...
better: I'm not able to lend money, but I hope you find a way soon. Can I help in another way?
also: I keep a rule of not lending money to friends. It protects the friendship.
weak: Arre, I'll check and tell you.
Sorry, sorry, I'll try to arrange something.
why: A clear no is kinder than a vague maybe that leaves them waiting.

situation: Your manager asks you to take on a colleague's work while yours is already full.
say: Okay sir, I'll try to adjust somehow.
better: I can't take that on without dropping something. Should I push the vendor report to next week?
also: My plate is full. Which of my current tasks should move?
weak: Sir, why always me? Give it to someone else.
Yes sir, no problem, I'll stay late.
why: Shows the trade-off and lets the manager choose; firm, not defensive.

situation: A relative insists you attend a function you have no time for.
say: Haan aunty, I'll try to come, let's see.
better: Aunty, I won't be able to make it this time. I'll call to wish them, and I'll send a gift.
also: I can't come on Sunday, but I'd love to visit them next month.
weak: I'll definitely come, pakka!
I'm too busy for all these functions.
why: A warm, definite no beats a 'maybe' you will break.

situation: A colleague keeps asking you to cover for them when they leave early.
say: Okay, but please, this is the last time, haan.
better: I'm not comfortable covering for you anymore. If you need to leave early, please tell the manager directly.
also: I've done it a few times, but I can't keep doing it.
weak: Fine, go, I'll manage, as always.
You're so selfish, always running away.
why: Clear limit, no guilt trip, no insult.

situation: A salesperson keeps pushing a credit card you have already refused.
say: Not now, maybe later, I'll think about it.
better: No, thank you. I'm not interested, and I'd like you to remove my number from your list.
also: I've decided. Please don't call again.
weak: Okay, send me the details, I'll see.
Stop calling me, you people are a nuisance!
why: A short, final no ends the pressure; 'maybe' invites more calls.

situation: Your client wants extra features added free, outside the agreed scope.
say: Okay sir, we'll try to adjust in the same cost.
better: Happy to add those. They're outside our agreed scope, so I'll send a quote and timeline by tomorrow.
also: We can do it as phase two. Let me share the cost.
weak: That's not possible, sir, it's not in contract, sorry.
Okay, we'll manage, no extra charges.
why: Says yes to the work and no to doing it free, calmly.

situation: Your in-laws keep pushing you to have a child soon.
say: Haan, haan, let's see, God's wish.
better: We know you're excited, and we love that. This is our decision, and we'll share news when we're ready.
also: We'd rather not discuss this right now. Thank you for understanding.
weak: This is none of your business.
Soon, soon, very soon, don't worry.
why: Kind but closed: respects them, keeps the decision yours.

situation: A friend pressures you to drink at a party when you do not want to.
say: No yaar, actually, I have a headache, small issue.
better: I'm not drinking tonight. I'm having a great time though. Get me a lime soda?
also: No thanks, I'm good. Really.
weak: Okay, just one, only for you.
I'm not like you people, I don't drink.
why: No excuse needed; a cheerful, final no works best.

situation: Your team pushes to cut testing to meet a deadline, and you disagree.
say: Okay, as you all say, majority wins.
better: I hear the pressure, but I can't sign off without testing payments. Let's cut a smaller feature instead.
also: I'm holding firm on this. A payment bug will cost us more than a delay.
weak: Fine, but if anything breaks, don't blame me.
You all don't understand quality at all.
why: Holds the line, gives a reason, and offers another way.

situation: A neighbour keeps asking you to keep their parcels and keys.
say: Sure aunty, anytime, no problem at all.
better: I'm happy to help now and then, but I'm out most days, so I can't keep parcels regularly.
also: This week works, but please find another option going forward.
weak: Aunty, I'm not your watchman.
Okay, okay, give, what else.
why: Sets a limit while keeping the relationship warm.

situation: Your boss calls on a Sunday, during a family event, about non-urgent work.
say: Yes sir, tell me sir, I'm free.
better: I'm at a family function today. If it can wait, I'll handle it first thing Monday.
also: If it's urgent, I can take ten minutes now. Otherwise, Monday.
weak: Sir, it's Sunday! Can't you leave me alone one day?
Sorry sir, network is very bad here, call you later.
why: Polite and clear about your time, with an option for real urgency.

situation: A cousin asks you to lie to their parents about where they were.
say: Okay, but if I get caught, you're responsible.
better: I'm not going to lie for you. I'll keep quiet, but if they ask me directly, I'll tell the truth.
also: I care about you, but I won't lie to your parents.
weak: Fine, what should I say, tell me the story.
I'll tell them everything right now.
why: Clear about what you will and won't do, without betraying them.

situation: Someone asks you to review their work for free, again.
say: Haan, send, I'll see when I get time.
better: I can't do free reviews anymore, my time's limited. My rate is 1,500 per document if that works.
also: I've helped a few times, but I need to charge for reviews now.
weak: Sure, no worries, it's only small work.
Why should I always do your work?
why: Values your time openly instead of quietly resenting it.

situation: In a negotiation, the other side asks you to drop your price again.
say: Okay, okay, final, I'll give ten percent more discount.
better: This is already our best price. I can't go lower, but I can add free delivery.
also: The price stays. Let's see what else would make this work for you.
weak: Sir, please understand, we also have families.
Take it or leave it.
why: Holds the price calmly and offers something that costs you less.

situation: Your friend asks you to be a loan guarantor.
say: Let me ask my father and tell you.
better: I won't be able to stand guarantee. It's a rule I keep with everyone. I hope the loan works out.
also: I can't sign that, but I'm happy to help you compare loan options.
weak: Okay, send the papers, I'll sign.
Are you mad? I don't trust anyone with money.
why: A clear 'rule I keep' makes the no less personal.

situation: A senior colleague insists you redo a task their way, but yours is sound.
say: Okay sir, you're senior, you know better.
better: I've thought about it and I'd like to keep my approach. It's faster and passed all checks. Can I walk you through it?
also: I respect your experience, but here the data supports my way.
weak: Sir, your method is outdated.
Okay, I'll redo it, no problem.
why: Respectful but steady: reasons, evidence, and openness to discuss.

situation: You've said no once, and a friend keeps pushing: 'Come on, just this once.'
say: Okay fine, you're forcing me, so I'll do it.
better: I've already said no, and that's my answer. Let's talk about something else.
also: I know you want me to, but it's still a no.
weak: Why don't you ever listen? You're so irritating.
Let me think again, maybe...
why: Repeat the no calmly; you owe no new reason.

situation: A recruiter asks you to accept an offer on the spot.
say: Okay, I'll join, I don't want to lose this chance.
better: Thank you, I'm interested. I'll give you my decision by Thursday after reviewing the offer properly.
also: I need two days to decide. I'll confirm by Thursday.
weak: Why so much hurry? Is something wrong with the company?
Can I tell you next month?
why: Takes the time you need, with a clear date.

situation: A family elder asks you to give up your weekend to run their errands, again.
say: Okay, okay, what's the point of my weekend anyway.
better: I can do the bank work on Saturday morning, but the rest of the weekend I need for myself.
also: I'll help with one thing this weekend. Which matters most?
weak: I'm always the one, why can't others help?
No, I'm busy, ask someone else.
why: Says yes to part, no to the rest; helpful and protective of your time.

situation: Your team lead wants you to give a fake positive update to the client.
say: Okay, as you say, I'll manage it somehow.
better: I'm not comfortable telling the client we're on track. Let's share the delay honestly with a recovery plan.
also: I'd rather give them bad news now than a bigger shock later.
weak: That's lying, I won't be part of your drama.
Fine, but it's on you, not me.
why: Refuses the lie and offers a better path, without accusing.

situation: A friend wants you to join a business scheme you don't trust.
say: Haan, sounds nice, I'll think and tell you.
better: Thanks for thinking of me, but I'm going to pass. It's not something I'm comfortable investing in.
also: It's a no from me, but I hope it goes well for you.
weak: These schemes are all frauds, you're getting cheated.
Okay, maybe I'll put a small amount.
why: A clear no without lecturing them about their choice.

situation: Your manager wants you to cancel your approved leave for a meeting.
say: Okay sir, I'll cancel, no issue.
better: My leave was approved last month and I have travel booked. I can join a short call that morning if it's essential.
also: I'll brief Anil before I go, so he can cover the meeting.
weak: Sir, this always happens, I never get leave.
Fine, I'll cancel and lose the tickets.
why: Holds to the agreed plan and still offers a reasonable fix.

situation: Someone you just met asks how much you earn.
say: Haha, not much yaar, just okay okay.
better: I'd rather keep that private, but I'm happy to talk about the work itself.
also: I keep salary stuff private. What do you do?
weak: Why do you want to know? That's so rude.
Around 18 lakhs, why, what's yours?
why: Polite, light and clear; no lie and no lecture.

situation: During a debate, people shout to make you change your view.
say: Okay, okay, maybe you all are right.
better: I hear you, and I still see it differently. Shouting won't change my mind; a good reason might.
also: Let's lower our voices. I'm open to evidence, not pressure.
weak: You all are idiots, I won't argue with you.
Whatever, think what you want.
why: Stays open to reasons but not to pressure.

situation: Your friend wants to stay at your place for a month, and you can't host.
say: Yaar, actually there's some problem, my landlord, you know...
better: I can't host you for a month, it's too long for my space. I can do this weekend while you find a place.
also: A month won't work for me, but let me share some PG contacts.
weak: Sure, come, stay as long as you want.
No, I don't like guests.
why: Honest limit plus real help beats a made-up excuse.
